text: Liu Pan is fierce and brave, and the border counties will soon learn to fear his raids. Ferocity builds with every attack, every sacked town and every executed captive, and fades whenever his riders sit idle behind the walls of Lingxian.

Liu Biao gave his nephew a free hand on the Changsha frontier. Loyal service keeps Xiangyang's coin and goodwill flowing; unchecked raiding and sacking make the uncle wonder what his kinsman is really building down south.

Ferocity is Liu Pan's raiding momentum: attacks, sacking and executions raise it, idleness lowers it.
Liu Biao's Favour measures how far Xiangyang still trusts its nephew on the frontier.

Liu Pan's riders wait behind the walls of Lingxian. Nobody across the border has heard from him in a season.
Scouts range across the border again. The raiders ride a little faster and come home a little richer.
Border towns bar their gates at dusk. Supplies are taken from the land, and the men fight harder on foreign soil, though the peasants at home grumble at the levies.
Enemy captains speak Liu Pan's name with irritation. His columns replenish in enemy land and strike from ambush, but Xiangyang begins to ask what its nephew is doing down south.
Whole counties are reorganised just to contain him. Every raid is faster, richer and better hidden, and Liu Biao's patience grows thinner with each one.
It would take a general of rare quality to hold him now. The Changsha bands are cheap to keep and impossible to catch, and the uncle who set him loose no longer trusts him.
Xiangyang has stopped answering Liu Pan's letters. No coin, no goodwill, and a court that quietly wonders whether the nephew has gone his own way.
Liu Biao lets his nephew be. The frontier is quiet enough, and quiet is all the governor of Jing asks for.
The uncle is pleased. Grain and coin move south a little more freely, and levies are easier to raise in Liu Biao's name.
Liu Biao names his nephew first among the border commanders. A stipend rides down from Xiangyang each season and the court speaks well of Changsha.
Some at Xiangyang whisper that the nephew would make a better heir than the sons. Liu Biao's treasury and his best replacements flow to the frontier without question.
Liu Pan serves as his uncle's vassal on the Changsha frontier. Favour grows each turn while the bond holds.
Liu Pan no longer answers to Xiangyang. Whatever favour remained is spent.
Plunder the local region for supplies. Liu Pan's Ferocity grows with every turn his riders spend raiding.
• Ferocity rises with attacking victories, sacked settlements, executed captives and armies in the Raiding stance, and decays while Liu Pan's riders sit idle.
• High Ferocity grants campaign movement, loot, supplies from raiding, replenishment in foreign land and ambush chance, at the cost of public order and Liu Biao's Favour.
• Liu Biao's Favour grows each turn while Liu Pan remains his uncle's vassal and when he defeats Liu Biao's enemies; sacking and unchecked ferocity erode it.
• High Favour brings income, cheaper recruitment, satisfaction and a stipend from Xiangyang; lose it and the frontier is on its own.
